partners.mechanism_chain: BBS1 (HGNC:1176) —DISRUPTS→ cilium assembly (GO:0031012); cilium assembly (GO:0031012) —LEADS_TO→ autophagy (GO:0006914); autophagy (GO:0006914) —LEADS_TO→ Bardet-Biedl syndrome (MONDO:0008854); TCP1 (HGNC:11656) —DISRUPTS→ autophagy (GO:0006914); autophagy (GO:0006914) —LEADS_TO→ intellectual developmental disorder with polymicrogyria and seizures (MONDO:0976124). **Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5620922)

**Proposed mechanism:** BBS1 (HGNC:1175) —DISRUPTS→ ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0060004); ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0060004) —LEADS_TO→ Retinitis pigmentosa (HP:0000547); ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0060004) —LEADS_TO→ Obesity (HP:0005175); SMO (HGNC:10961) —DISRUPTS→ ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0060004); ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0060004) —LEADS_TO→ Postaxial polydactyly (HP:0001153); ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0060004) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Mutations in BBS1 disrupt ciliary protein trafficking, leading to phenotypes like retinitis pigmentosa and obesity in Bardet-Biedl syndrome. Haploinsufficiency of SMO also disrupts ciliary protein trafficking, affecting Hedgehog signaling and leading to phenotypes such as postaxial polydactyly and intellectual disability in Curry-Jones syndrome. The shared disruption of ciliary protein trafficking serves as the mechanistic link.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that SMO is not a component of the BBSome complex or that its trafficking to cilia is independent of BBS proteins would falsify this hypothesis.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ciliary protein trafficking in these distinct syndromes could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both BBS and Curry-Jones syndrome, potentially involving modulators of the Hedgehog pathway or general ciliary function.

#### 10. basal cell carcinoma, susceptibility to, 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.293)

This convergence on Hedgehog signaling pathway dysregulation forms the mechanistic link.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in PTCH1 do not lead to constitutive activation of the Hedgehog pathway in relevant cell types, or that BBS1 mutations do not impact ciliogenesis or downstream signaling pathways that intersect with Hedgehog signaling. _(variant: Exclusion of pathogenic variants in PTCH1 (for BCC) and BBS1 (for BBS) from common population databases (e.g., gnomAD frequency > 1% for pathogenic variants).)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the Hedgehog signaling pathway in both Bardet-Biedl syndrome and basal cell carcinoma susceptibility could reveal novel therapeutic targets.
